positive_feedback: verify.rs implements C1-C5 exactly as specified: C1 (@strict discipline) walks the raw AST because HIR no-ops @strict (lower.rs:167), correctly emitting strict_missing_intent/complexity/precondition per-element rather than one blob error. C2(a) maps every relevant HirError (UnsupportedDebugPredicate, PreconditionOperandNotScalar, TooManyDebugConditions, UnsupportedPrecondition) to precise codes. C2(b)'s arity-drop scan is a straight args.len()!=1 walk with a differential AT-2883b pin against lower.rs's actual drop predicate -- a real anti-drift guard, not just an assertion of the tool's own output. C3 correctly reuses the ALREADY-COMPUTED HIR two-tier threshold (PORTABLE_MIN=128 warn / DESKTOP_MAX=1024 hard-error) instead of inventing a new one -- and the coder honestly substituted the fixture's workgroup product (256) for the spec's own inconsistent 2048 illustrative example, documented inline and confirmed correct by QA's direct read of hir.rs/validate.rs.

verify_source is genuinely pure (no fs/Vulkan) with `Error` correctly reserved for the CLI layer (an unreadable file never reaches verify_source) -- this exact separation is asserted by AT-2887b via exit-code mapping and enforced by run_verify's io-error branch in main.rs.

fuzz.rs's interval satisfier (IntDomain/FloatDomain) matches the spec's flip-table, i128 exact-integer arithmetic, and f32-only float pipeline (r3/C-1new) line for line -- adjust_open_lower's f32::MIN_POSITIVE floor for the alpha>0 case and next_up()/next_down() for general open bounds are exactly the r2/M-1 + r3/C-1new fix, with a dedicated AT-2890 unit sweeping 64 runs asserting the open-lower sample is always strictly >0.

classify_run is the real deal: a genuine 4-branch match producing all 4 quadrants of the r3/fix-4 table, a deferred-condition exemption computed via a separate bitmask BEFORE quadrant classification (constrained_mask/deferred_mask), and a single severity_rank()-driven fold (candidates.sort_by_key + .next()) that mechanically enforces the r4 orchestrator's ERROR>FAIL>UNCONSTRAINED>PASS ordering for BOTH intra-run signal composition and (via record_worst, same severity_rank) cross-run aggregation -- not two independently-hand-rolled precedence rules that could drift apart. AT-2891's 4 quadrant units + AT-2892's deferred-exemption unit + the r4 composition unit (deferred fire + real postcondition violation in the same run resolves to FAIL, not UNCONSTRAINED_PRECONDITION_FIRED) are all present and correctly assert the exact reason_kind/exit code per cell.

The zero-compiler-change gate holds by construction: `git diff main...HEAD -- crates/axc-lexer crates/axc-parser crates/axc-hir crates/axc-codegen crates/axc-runtime` is empty (independently re-confirmed), and the one driver-crate edit (rewrite_verify.rs's find_nondeterminism -> pub(crate)) is a visibility-only bump exactly per spec §5/M-2 -- reused verbatim by fuzz.rs's determinism leg (c) rather than duplicated.

The oracle wiring is correct and matches the r2/C-1 fix precisely: every dispatch call in fuzz.rs's debug path goes through dispatch_debug_checked; the non-debug-oracle smoke path correctly uses the raw vk.dispatch() (DispatchRequest), never the flag-blind dispatch_handle. AT-2897 is a real, deliberately-engineered 'always-pass-oracle guard' -- a postcondition that MUST fire, which a dispatch_handle-style mis-wire could not pass.

cli.rs's two new subcommands (Verify, Test) follow the RewriteVerify precedent exactly (PathBuf input, --json / --fuzz mode flags, StrategyValue reuse, clap doc comments naming the exit-code contract) and AT-2875c/AT-2894c-style cross-subcommand negative tests (no OTHER subcommand exposes --fuzz/--debug) are present for the new flags too (at_2894c_no_other_subcommand_exposes_fuzz).

The QA-blocking fix (commit 64b47b8) is exactly scoped: main.rs::run_test's buffer-size usage gate is reordered to thread an empty Vec through fuzz_kernel rather than usage-erroring pre-emptively, letting fuzz_kernel's own solve()-based UNSATISFIABLE short-circuit run first. The fuzz.rs diff in that commit is test-rename/doc-comment only (verified via git diff -- 15 lines, all inside mod tests). New tests/fuzz_cli.rs drives the REAL built binary as a subprocess (the rewrite_verify_cli.rs convention) and closes exactly the coverage gap QA identified, including a regression guard (AT-2893b) that a satisfiable kernel missing size flags still usage-errors.

verdict-first-key JSON discipline (serde struct-field-order technique) is followed consistently in both VerifyReport and FuzzReport, and is asserted in both CPU unit tests and the CLI subprocess test (stdout.trim_start().starts_with("{\n  \"verdict\"")).

Anti-pattern #4 (exhaustive matches, no silent wildcard) is respected in the places that matter most: the Item::Kernel match in verify.rs, hir_warning_span's per-variant match, and decode_scalar_json's all-12-ScalarTy match (confirmed necessary breadth, not padding, since §3.4 fuzzes every kernel scalar param, not just DebugCheck-restricted ones).

minor_issues.description: classify_hir_warning uses a catch-all `other => (Category::Other, "hir_warning", format!("{other:?}"))` arm rather than an exhaustive per-variant match, which is a slight style inconsistency next to hir_warning_span's fully exhaustive match three functions above it. Not a correctness issue (nothing is silently dropped -- every warning is still surfaced, just under a generic code/category for variants outside C3/C4's scope), and it is arguably the right call here since verify's contract is 'surface everything, categorize only what has a named check' -- but a future HirWarning variant addition will not force a compile-time revisit the way the exhaustive matches elsewhere in this file do. Cosmetic; not blocking.

ROADMAP.md/DESIGN.md are not updated in this branch to mark FG.8 done. Confirmed this is NOT a deviation from project convention: M3.16 and M3.17 both landed their ROADMAP-status-flip in a separate 'docs(M3.1X)' commit AFTER the merge commit, not inside the feature branch (git log shows 1eaaa67 'docs(M3.17): ROADMAP -- FG.4 done' following the M3.17 merge). Flagging only so the orchestrator schedules the equivalent docs(M3.18) follow-up commit at close-out, per precedent -- not a defect in this branch.

QA's independent LOC audit found product-only code (1785 LOC) already ~32% over the spec's own product-only estimate (~1355 total incl. tests), and grand total (2581) is ~1.52x the stated hard cap (1700). QA traced the overage to fuzz.rs's satisfier+orchestration (+402 over estimate) and test thoroughness (+487 over estimate, from multi-sub-case-per-AT coverage), confirmed NOT duplication via a reuse-vs-reinvention grep sweep (seeded_inputs/derive_workgroups/find_nondeterminism all correctly reused, not reimplemented). I independently spot-read the largest single file (fuzz.rs, 1487 lines) end to end and agree: every substantial function maps to a named spec section (§3.2b discriminator, §3.3 violate-eligibility, §3.4 satisfier) with no dead/speculative code. Treating this as an honest, disclosed miss on the Architect's own r3 estimate (the discriminator totality + deferred-exemption + severity-ordering machinery was added across r2/r3/r4 without a proportional LOC-budget bump) rather than a Coder discipline failure -- consistent with QA's own framing. Not blocking; a retroactive trim pass on fuzz.rs is a reasonable but non-mandatory follow-up.

test_coverage_assessment: AT-2881..2899 (all 19) are present and each maps to a specific, correctly-scoped test: CPU-only checks (verify.rs, fuzz.rs satisfier/discriminator units) are genuinely pure and synthetic-input-driven per the spec's 'no GPU, no compile' mandate for the satisfier; GPU ATs (2896-2899) in fuzz_gpu.rs are #[ignore]-gated per project convention and independently re-verified green by QA on both real NVIDIA and Lavapipe, including a 6/6 independent re-measurement of AT-2897's pinned (seed,window,runs) triple to confirm genuine (not lucky) determinism. The post-QA fix added a correctly-scoped CLI-subprocess-level AT-2893 test that closes the exact gap the original unit test's library-level shortcut had masked, with an honest doc-comment trail explaining why the original test's name overclaimed 'end-to-end' coverage.
spec_deviations_found: None that are unjustified. The one documented deviation (AT-2885's fixture value: 256 instead of the spec's illustrative 2048) is required by a pre-existing, frozen HIR threshold (DESKTOP_MAX_WORKGROUP_INVOCATIONS=1024) that this milestone cannot touch without breaching the zero-compiler-change gate -- correctly flagged inline in both the coder's fixture comment and QA's independent hir.rs/validate.rs read.
summary: M3.18 delivers axc verify (C1-C5) and axc test --fuzz (satisfier + oracle triad + 4-quadrant discriminator + severity-ordered verdict) exactly per the r4-final spec, reusing the M3.17 debug-check runtime and M3.16 determinism-check verbatim with zero compiler-crate diff. The satisfier, discriminator, and severity-ordering logic are implemented as real, unit-tested pure functions rather than ad-hoc branching, and match the spec's r2/r3/r4 fixes (f32-only float pipeline, open-bound strict-interior sampling, TOTAL 4-quadrant discriminator, deferred-condition exemption, verdict-precedence ordering) precisely. The single QA-blocking finding (CLI-level buffer-size gate pre-empting the UNSATISFIABLE short-circuit for AT-2893's literal spec command) was fixed with a minimal, correctly-scoped reorder plus new subprocess-level CLI tests, and QA's re-check confirms the fix, the preserved usage-gate behavior, and zero regression across the full workspace test suite plus real-GPU spot-checks. The LOC overage (~1.52x the stated cap) is real but independently confirmed non-duplicative and scope-driven; it does not affect correctness or spec compliance. APPROVE.
